nodes.statement: A {\bf hyperplane} is the perp space of a point. A {\bf halfspace} is the dual of a point. The dimension of the module the cone is a submodule of. The {\bf dimension} of a pointed cone. A polyhedral cone is {\bf full-dimensional} if its dimension is the same as the dimension of the ambient space. The set of all \(k\)-dimensional faces of a polyheadral cone. For each \(k\) gives the number of \(k\)-dimensional faces of a polyheadral cone.
nodes.label: names

nodes.statement: A {\bf pointed cone} \( \sigma \subseteq N \) is a \( \Bbbk_{\geq 0} \)-submodule of \( N \).
nodes.label: pointed-cone

nodes.statement: A {\bf pointy cone} \( \sigma \subseteq N \) is a \( \Bbbk_{\geq 0} \)-submodule of \( N \) that does not contain a nontrivial linear space.
nodes.label: pointy-cone

nodes.statement: For a set \( S \subseteq N \), the {\bf cone generated by \( S \)} is the pointed cone \[ \mathrm{Cone}(S) := \mathrm{Span}_{\Bbbk_{\geq 0}}(S) \subseteq N. \]
nodes.label: cone-span

nodes.statement: A pointed cone \( \sigma \subseteq N \) is called {\bf finitely generated}, if \( \sigma = \mathrm{Cone}(S) \) for some finite set \( S \subseteq N \).
nodes.label: cone-finitely-generated

nodes.statement: For a set \( S \subseteq M \), the {\bf dual cone of \( S \)} is the pointed cone \[ S^\vee := \{x \in N \mid \forall y \in S, \langle x, y \rangle \geq 0 \} \subseteq N. \]
nodes.label: dual-cone

nodes.statement: Another word for finitely generated cone with a finitely generated canonical dual.
nodes.label: polyhedral-cone

nodes.statement: The zero-space \( \{0\} \subseteq N \) is a polyhedral cone.
nodes.label: bot-polyhedral

nodes.statement: If \( S \subseteq M \) is a finite \( \Bbbk \)-basis of \( M \), then \( \{0\} = (S \cup -S)^\vee \).
The full space is a polyhedral cone.
nodes.label: all-polyhedral-cone

nodes.statement: Any halfspace is a polyhedral cone.
nodes.label: halfspace-polyhedral-cone

nodes.statement: Any linear subspace is a polyhedral cone.
nodes.label: linear-subspace-polyhedral-cone

nodes.statement: If \( \sigma \subset N \) is finitely generated, then \( \sigma^\vee \subset M \) is polyhedral.
nodes.label: dual-polyhedral

nodes.statement: Let \( \sigma = \mathrm{Cone}(S) \) for \( S \subseteq N \). We need to show \( \mathrm{Cone}(S)^\vee = S^\vee \). The inclusion ``\( \subseteq \)'' is obvious, as \( S \subseteq \mathrm{Cone}(S) \). The opposite inclusion can be shown by induction on the general element of \( \mathrm{Cone}(S) \).

nodes.name: Double dual
nodes.statement: If \( \sigma \subseteq N \) is polyhedral, then \( \sigma^{\vee\vee} = \sigma \).
nodes.label: double-dual-polyhedral-cone

nodes.statement: For any set \( S \subseteq N \) it is trivial to show \( S^{\vee\vee\vee} = S^{\vee} \). The claim follows since \( \sigma = S^{\vee} \) for a finite set \( S \subseteq N \).

nodes.name: Fourier-Motkin elimination
nodes.statement: If \( \sigma \subseteq N \) is a polyhedral cone and \( w \in N \), then \( \sigma + \mathrm{Cone}(\{w\}) \) is polyhedral too.
nodes.label: fourier-motzkin

nodes.statement: Write \( \sigma = S^{\vee} \) for a finite \( S \subseteq M \). Define \[ T\ :=\ \{x \in S \mid 0 \leq \langle x, w \rangle \}\ \cup\ \{y \langle x, w \rangle - x \langle y, w \rangle \mid x, y \in S, 0 \leq \langle x, w \rangle, \langle y, w \rangle < 0 \}\ \subseteq\ M. \] Note that \( T \) is finite. We claim \( S^{\vee} + \mathrm{Cone}(\{w\}) = T^{\vee} \). Clearly \( T \subseteq \mathrm{Cone}(S) \), hence \( S^{\vee} = \mathrm{Cone}(S)^{\vee} \subseteq T^{\vee} \). Also clear is \( w \in T^{\vee} \), hence \( S^{\vee} + \mathrm{Cone}(\{w\}) \subset T^{\vee} \). For the reverse inclusion, let \( v \in T^\vee \). We need to show \( v - uw \in S^\vee \) for some \( u \in \Bbbk_{\geq 0} \). If there is no \( y \in S \) with both \( \langle y, w \rangle < 0 \) and \( \langle y, v \rangle < 0 \), we can easily see that \( u = 0 \) works, i.e. \( T^{\vee} \subseteq S^{\vee} \). Otherwise, we set \[ u\ :=\ \max_{\substack{y \in S \\ \langle y, w \rangle < 0}} \frac{\langle y, v \rangle}{\langle y, w \rangle}, \] which is then well-defined and non-negative. We need to show \( u \langle z, w \rangle \leq \langle z, v \rangle \) for all \( z \in S \). If \( \langle z, w \rangle < 0 \), this follows from maximality of \( u \). If \( \langle z, w \rangle = 0 \), the claim follows from \( z \in T \) and \( v \in T^{\vee} \). Lastly, assume \( \langle z, w \rangle > 0 \) and fix \( y \in S \) such that \( u = \frac{\langle y, v \rangle}{\langle y, w \rangle} \). In particular, \( \langle y, w \rangle < 0 \). Then the claim \( u \langle z, w \rangle \leq \langle z, v \rangle \) is equivalent to \[ \langle y, v \rangle \langle z, w \rangle \geq \langle z, v \rangle \langle y, w \rangle. \] But \( y \langle z, w \rangle - z \langle y, w \rangle \in T \), hence the claim follows from \( v \in T^{\vee} \).
If \( \sigma \in N \) is finitely generated, then it is polyhedral.
nodes.label: polyhedral-of-fg

nodes.statement: Write \( \sigma = \mathrm{Cone}(S) \) and use induction on the size of \( S \): For \( S = \emptyset \), we use~\ref{bot-polyhedral} and the induction step is~\ref{fourier-motzkin}.
For a finite set \( S \subseteq N \), we have \( S^{\vee\vee} = \mathrm{Cone}(S) \).
nodes.label: double-dual-finite-set

nodes.statement: The cone \( \sigma := \mathrm{Cone}(S) \) is finitely generated, hence polyhedral by~\ref{polyhedral-of-fg}. Furthermore, we have \( \sigma^{\vee\vee} = S^{\vee\vee} \). Now apply~\ref{double-dual-polyhedral-cone}.

nodes.name: Polyhedral = Finitely generated
nodes.statement: A pointed cone \( \sigma \subseteq N \) is finitely generated iff it is polyhedral.
nodes.label: polyhedral-iff-fg

nodes.statement: The implication ``\( \Rightarrow \)'' is Proposition~\ref{polyhedral-of-fg}. For the converse, assume \( \sigma = S^{\vee} \) for some finite \( S \subseteq M \). Then \( \mathrm{Cone}(S) \) is finitely generated, hence polyhedral by~\ref{polyhedral-of-fg}. Thus we find a finite \( T \subseteq N \) with \( \mathrm{Cone}(S) = T^\vee \). We obtain \[ \sigma = S^{\vee} = \mathrm{Cone}(S)^\vee = T^{\vee\vee} = \mathrm{Cone}(T), \] where the last equality is due to~\ref{double-dual-finite-set}. Thus \( \sigma \) is finitely generated.
If \( \sigma \subseteq N \) is polyhedral, then \( \sigma^\vee \subseteq M \) is polyhedral too.
nodes.label: dual-polyhedral-cone

nodes.statement: \ref{dual-polyhedral} \( + \) \ref{polyhedral-iff-fg}.
Every polyhedral cone can be written as the minkowski sum of a pointy cone and a linear subspace.
nodes.label: pointy-linear-sum-polyhedral-cone

nodes.statement: If \( \sigma \subseteq N \) is polyhedral and \(f : N -> M\) is a linear map, then \( f.map \sigma \subseteq M \) is polyhedral too.
nodes.label: linear-transformation-polyhedral-cone

nodes.statement: If \( \sigma, \tau \subseteq N \) are polyhedral, then \( \sigma + \tau \) is polyhedral too.
nodes.label: sum-polyhedral-cone

nodes.statement: If \( \sigma, \tau \subseteq N \) are polyhedral, the direct sum \( \sigma \oplus_p \tau \) is polyhedral too.
nodes.label: direct-sum-polyhedral-cone

nodes.statement: If \( \sigma, \tau \subseteq N \) are polyhedral, their join is polyhedral too.
nodes.label: join-polyhedral-cone

nodes.statement: If \( \sigma, \tau \subseteq N \) are polyhedral, then \( \sigma \cap \tau \) is polyhedral too.
nodes.label: intersection-polyhedral-cone

nodes.statement: If \( \sigma, \tau \subseteq N \) are polyhedral, then the cartesian product \( \sigma \prod \tau \) is polyhedral too.
nodes.label: product-polyhedral-cone

nodes.name: Convex hull
nodes.statement: For a set $S \subseteq N$, the {\bf convex hull of $S$} is $$\mathrm{Conv}(S) := \left\{\sum_{u \in S} \lambda_u | \lambda_u \ge 0, \sum_u \lambda_u = 1\right\}$$
nodes.label: convex-hull

nodes.statement: If \( \sigma, \tau \subseteq N \) are polyhedral, then the convex hull of the two is polyhedral too.
nodes.label: convex-hull-polyhedral-cone

nodes.statement: Polyhedral cones for a lattice under intersections and convex hulls (its the same lattice as on pointed cones).
nodes.label: polyhedra-lattice

nodes.statement: A simplicial cone \(\sigma\) is a polyhedral cone that can be generated by \(dim (\sigma)\) many generators.
nodes.label: simplicial-cone

nodes.statement: For any subset \( A \subseteq M \), we define the \emph{perp space} \[ A^{\perp}\ :=\ \{v \in N\ \mid\ \forall u \in A, \langle v, u \rangle = 0\}, \] which is a pointed cone in \( N \). We also write \( u^{\perp} := \{u\}^{\perp} \).
nodes.label: perp

nodes.statement: If \( A \subseteq M \) is closed under negation (for instance, \( A \subseteq M \) a \( \Bbbk \)-submodule), then \( A^{\perp} = A^{\vee} \).
nodes.label: perp-closed-negation

nodes.statement: \( A^{\perp} \subseteq A^{\vee} \) is clear. Let \( x \in A^{\vee} \) and \( a \in A \). then \( \langle x, a \rangle \geq 0 \) and \( -\langle x, a \rangle = \langle x, -a \rangle \geq 0 \). Hence \( \langle x, a \rangle = 0 \) and \( x \in A^{\perp} \).

nodes.name: Face of a cone
nodes.statement: A \emph{face} of a pointed cone \( \sigma \subseteq N \) is the intersection of \( \sigma \) with some hyperplane \( u^{\perp} \) for \( u \in \sigma^{\vee} \). We write \( \tau \preceq \sigma \) if \( \tau \) is a face of \( \sigma \) and \( \tau \prec \sigma \) if \( \tau \) is a \emph{proper} face, i.e. \( \tau \preceq \sigma \) and \( \tau \neq \sigma \).
nodes.label: face

nodes.statement: For any subset \( S \subseteq N \) and \( u \in S^{\vee} \), we have \[ \mathrm{Cone}(S) \cap u^{\perp} = \mathrm{Cone}(S \cap u^{\perp}). \]
nodes.label: cone-inter-perp

nodes.statement: Both inclusions should be a simple Span-induction.
A face of a polyhedral cone is polyhedral.
nodes.label: face-polyhedral

nodes.statement: Use \ref{cone-inter-perp} and the fact that if \( S \) is finite, so is \( S \cap u^{\perp} \).
A polyhedral cone has only finitely many faces.
nodes.label: faces-polyhedral-cone-finite

nodes.statement: By \ref{face-polyhedral}, a face of a polyhedral cone \( \sigma = \mathrm{Cone}(S) \) is of the form \( \mathrm{Cone}(S') \) for some \( S' \subseteq S \). Being finite, \( S \) has only finitely many subsets, which shows the claim.

nodes.name: Intersection of faces
nodes.statement: If \( \sigma \) is a pointed cone, then the intersection of two faces of \( \sigma \) is a again face of \( \sigma \).
nodes.label: face-intersection

nodes.statement: Let \( \tau = \sigma \cap u^{\perp} \) and \( \tau' = \sigma \cap \tau'^{\perp} \) be faces. We claim that \( \sigma \cap u^{\perp} \cap u'^{\perp} = \sigma \cap (u + u')^{\perp} \). The inclusion ``\( \subseteq \)'' is obvious. For the converse, suppose \( v \in \sigma \) with \( \langle v, u \rangle + \langle v, u' \rangle = 0 \). Since \( u, u' \in \sigma^{\vee} \), both summands are nonnegative, hence \( \langle v, u \rangle = \langle v, u' \rangle = 0 \).
Let \( \tau \preceq \sigma \) be a face of a pointed cone. Then \( \tau^{\vee} = \tau^{\perp} + \sigma^{\vee} \).
nodes.label: face-dual-eq-sum

nodes.statement: It's easy to show that \( \tau = \mathrm{Span}_{\Bbbk}(\tau) \cap \sigma^{\vee} \). Dualising gives \( \tau^{\vee} = \mathrm{Span}_{\Bbbk}(\tau)^{\vee} + \sigma^{\vee} \). Apply~\ref{perp-closed-negation} to get \( \mathrm{Span}_{\Bbbk}(\tau)^{\vee} = \mathrm{Span}_{\Bbbk}(\tau)^{\perp} = \tau^{\perp} \).

nodes.name: Face of a face
nodes.statement: A face of a face of a polyhedral cone \( \sigma \) is again a face of \( \sigma \).
nodes.label: face-face

nodes.statement: Let \( \tau = \sigma \cap u^{\perp} \) with \( u \in \sigma^{\vee} \) and \( \rho = \tau \cap v^{\perp} \) with \( v \in \tau^{\vee} \). By \ref{face-dual-eq-sum}, we can write \( v = v_1 + v_2 \) with \( v_1 \in \tau^{\perp} \) and \( v_2 \in \sigma^{\vee} \). Then \( u + v_2 \in \sigma^{\vee} \) and we claim \( \rho = \sigma \cap (u + v_2)^{\perp} \). For ``\( \subseteq \)'', let \( x \in \rho = \tau \cap v^{\perp} \). Since \( x \in \tau \), we get \( \langle x, u \rangle = 0 \) and \( \langle x, v_1 \rangle = 0 \). Since \( x \in v^{\perp} \), also \( \langle x, v \rangle = 0 \), which by \( v = v_1 + v_2 \) implies \( \langle x, v_2 \rangle = 0 \). In total, \( \langle x, u + v_2 \rangle = 0 \). For the converse, assume \( x \in \sigma \cap (u + v_2)^{\perp} \), i.e. \( \langle x, u \rangle + \langle x, v_2 \rangle = 0 \). Since both \( u, v_2 \in \sigma^{\vee} \) and \( x \in \sigma \), both summands are nonnegative, hence \( \langle x, u \rangle = \langle x, v_2 \rangle = 0 \). This implies \( x \in \tau \), thus also \( \langle x, v_1 \rangle = 0 \). In total, \( \langle x, v \rangle = \langle x, v_1 \rangle + \langle x, v_2 \rangle = 0 \), thus \( x \in \rho \).

nodes.name: Face order is a lattice
nodes.statement: Given a polyhedral cone, the partial order on its faces is a lattice. We call it the \emph{face lattice} of the cone.
nodes.label: face-lattice

nodes.statement: Top is the entire cone, bot is the empty cone.

nodes.name: Face lattice is graded
nodes.statement: Given a polyhedral cone, the partial order on its faces is graded.
nodes.label: face-lattice-graded

nodes.statement: The grading is given by the number of faces of this face.

nodes.name: Combinatorial Equivalence
nodes.statement: Two polyhedral cones are \emph{combinatorially equivalent} if there is an order isomorphism between their face lattices.
nodes.label: combinatorial-equivalence

nodes.statement: Face lattices of dual cones are dual to each other.
nodes.label: dual-face-lattice

nodes.statement: The face lattice of a face is isomorphic to a lower interval of the face lattice of a polyhedral cone.
nodes.label: face-face-lattice

nodes.statement: Linear transformaions preserve combinatorial equivalence. There is an iso that should be provided
nodes.label: ombinatorial-equivalence-linear-transformaions

nodes.name: Polar Cone
nodes.statement: For a pointed cone \( \sigma \), the {\bf polar cone of \( \sigma \)} is the pointed cone \[ S^\circ := \{x \in \sigma \mid \forall y \in \sigma, \langle x, y \rangle \leq 0 \} \]
nodes.label: polar-cone

nodes.name: Polytope
nodes.statement: A {\bf polytope} is a set that can be written as $\mathrm{Conv}(S)$ for some finite set $S$.
nodes.label: polytope
